title: In One Ear: Sasquatch awareness

content:
Published 6:00 am Thursday, October 22, 2026

The Ear missed National Sasquatch Awareness Day on Oct. 20, the date of the Patterson-Gimlin 1967 film of the trudging sasquatch in Northern California (long believed to be a hoax).

Even so, the sasquatch sightings keep rolling in at the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization. The latest Class A sighting was at noon on May 10, a clear day, near Carson, Washington, from about 40 feet away at the closest point.

“I was driving in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest … I noticed debris falling from the bank of the road and a large bolder in the ditch,” the driver wrote. “I looked up (and) saw a reddish-brown furry figure standing at the edge of the embankment. The terrain behind it was heavy forestation.

“Because I was driving, it is hard to say the height, and I did not see a face. It may have had its back to me, but it was standing upright and definitely not human or a bear … I just know that there have been sightings in this region. I was not looking for bigfoot, but this was the only explanation for what I saw.”

In case you’re wondering, Washington has the most sightings overall at 734; Oregon only has 262. (Screenshot: Patterson family via New York Post)
